title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, eyes on Warsh
source_used: AFP (text read on Yahoo Finance, whose page names AFP as the provider)
key_facts: Most Asian markets rose on Friday 16 Oct 2026 after Thursday's tech rout over concerns about the AI boom.
Seoul rose more than 2% and Tokyo about 1.8% after falling 7.6% and 4.9% on Thursday.
Traders awaited remarks from Federal Reserve head Kevin Warsh at the IMF gathering in Bangkok.
CoreWeave, a New Jersey firm that borrowed heavily to buy Nvidia chips, fell 15.5% Wednesday as some bond yields soared.
Nvidia chief Jensen Huang told Bloomberg that 'CoreWeave's strength is improving every day' and that its cost of capital is decreasing.
SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes said Huang's defence pulled the neocloud group off the floor.
US inflation was the highest in five months, lifting bets on a second straight rate hike this month.
quote_evidence: Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day's tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, with traders also awaiting comments from Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh at the IMF's annual gathering.
"CoreWeave's strength is improving every day," he told Bloomberg. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."
why_it_matters_hint: Asian markets rebounded as Nvidia's chief defended CoreWeave's finances.
notes: Pool source Yahoo Finance; the Yahoo page metadata names AFP as provider, so AFP is credited. Item is dated Friday 16 Oct 2026 and describes Thursday's rout.
